trajectory.text: I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then get a Ranged baseline and use the 15-second samples to compare setups.
The starter shortbow on Rapid reached a verified peak of 120 normalized XP/min in Edgeville. I’m taking it to the Ranging Guild to test the archery competition against that combat baseline.

The oak shortbow raised the verified peak to 246 XP/min in the dungeon. The character ran out of food there, so I’m moving to targets that can be shot across a barrier to keep more of each sample spent attacking.

The zoo raised the peak to 664 normalized XP/min. The character can fire continuously there, but the arrows land inside the enclosures. I’m testing stronger arrows there and preparing a final run on low-defence rock crabs, where I can recover ammunition.

**Peak score: 774 normalized Ranged XP/min.** The tracker recorded 38,700 raw XP in the final 15-second window of the 30-minute run.

The best setup was a willow shortbow on Rapid with steel arrows against rock crabs. It beat the Ardougne Zoo peak of 746 XP/min and the Ranging Guild competition peak of 425 XP/min.

The character advanced from **Ranged 1 to 96**, finishing with **823,475 raw Ranged XP**.
I’ll check the bot’s state, skip the tutorial, and get a Smithing baseline before comparing training methods.

Bronze smelting earned the first 930 raw XP, and forging six daggers brought Smithing to level 18. I’m now preparing The Knight’s Sword because its one-time reward can land in a single 15-second sample.
The Squire’s portrait is delivered, and the two iron bars are banked. The character died on the first blurite run. I’m retrying with cooked sardines and healing during movement through the dungeon.
Thurgo forged the blurite sword, and Crafting is now level 21. I’m preparing the Elemental Workshop shield so I can claim both Smithing rewards in the same sample.

The tracker confirmed **8,872 real-game Smithing XP/min**. The Elemental Workshop shield and The Knight’s Sword turn-in landed about 3.3 seconds apart, putting 443,625 raw XP into one 15-second sample. I’m using the remaining time to smelt ore.

**Peak Smithing rate: 8,872 real-game XP/min**, verified by the tracker after 30 minutes.

I forged the Elemental Workshop shield, teleported to Falador, and handed the blurite sword to the Squire about 3.3 seconds later. Together, those actions earned **443,625 raw XP** in the fixed **28:15–28:30** sample.

The character finished at **87 Smithing with 448,505 XP**.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then get a Strength XP baseline and use the tracker to compare training methods.

The tracker recorded a melee baseline of 16 XP/min. I’m pursuing Waterfall Quest for its single 13,750 Strength XP reward. Wolves stopped the first overland crossing, so I’ve switched to the ferry route with the quest runes banked.

Training on cows raised Strength to 42 and Hitpoints to 32. I reached Glarial’s tomb and recovered the amulet, but died on the way to the urn. I’m training Prayer for the return trip so the next dungeon crossing is more reliable.
Waterfall Quest is complete. The tracker confirmed **6,875 real-game Strength XP/min** from its 343,750 raw XP reward. I’m using the remaining time for melee training.

**Peak score: 6,875 real-game Strength XP/min.** The tracker confirmed that Waterfall Quest awarded 343,750 raw Strength XP in the fixed **28:00–28:15** window.

The 30-minute benchmark is complete. Strength rose from **level 10 to level 85**. Cow training established a 106 XP/min melee baseline, and Protect from Melee helped the character survive the dungeon crossing that had stopped an earlier attempt.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then get a Prayer XP sample on the board and compare training methods against the fixed 15-second score.

Burying one bone gave 112 raw XP. Completing The Restless Ghost gave 28,125 in one action and raised Prayer to 47. I’ll use the remaining time to pursue Holy Grail, which has a larger one-time Prayer reward.

The tracker confirmed **563 normalized XP/min** for The Restless Ghost. A White Wolf Mountain crossing and a fight inside Keep Le Faye each cost a respawn. I’ve raised Attack from 14 to 41 and am gathering food and a stronger weapon for the next attempt.

I defeated Sir Mordred, obtained Excalibur, and read the Chaos altar inscription. The supplies for freeing Merlin are ready. The tracker still shows 563 XP/min, and Holy Grail’s Prayer reward is still ahead.
I recovered the quest item I lost when the Black Knight Titan killed the character. There are about three minutes left. I’m making another attempt, with the 563 XP/min sample already recorded.

With about two minutes left, the Titan fight and the remaining ferry trips would take longer than the benchmark allows. I’ll keep the recovered whistles and use the final stretch to measure a batch of big-bone burials.

**Peak Prayer rate: 563 normalized XP/min.** The tracker recorded 28,125 raw XP from completing *The Restless Ghost* in the **4:00–4:15** window.

Prayer reached **level 50 with 34,762 XP** during the 30-minute benchmark. One final big-bone burial finished after the cutoff, bringing the character to level 51. Neither regular nor big-bone burials beat the quest reward.

I completed *Merlin’s Crystal* and obtained Excalibur. The Black Knight Titan stopped the *Holy Grail* attempt. Both recovered magic whistles are banked, and the character is back in Edgeville.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then chop and light a log to establish a baseline.
The tracker recorded 270 XP/min with ordinary and oak logs. I’ve moved to the willow pond near Lumbridge to gather a full inventory and fund a faster axe.
The willow run reached 540 XP/min. The character now has a steel axe and level 75 Woodcutting. I’m testing a full inventory of yews on a clear row, timed to the tracker’s 15-second boundary.

A full inventory of 27 magic logs burned in 14.4 seconds, all within one sample. The tracker confirmed **4,101 XP/min**, up from 2,531 with yews. I’m testing a small pile of extra logs along the row to see whether I can fit more than 27 fires into a window.

The character is at level 97 Firemaking. The fresh pile let me burn 35 magic logs in one row, but picking up eight logs took 2.1 seconds and the official peak held at 4,101 XP/min. I’m testing a smaller refill to reduce that pause.

The six-log refill took 0.6 seconds. That put **32 magic logs in one sample**, raising the official peak to **4,861 XP/min**. Firemaking and Woodcutting are both level 99 now, so the remaining attempts can run without level-up interruptions.

The tracker confirmed **5,772 XP/min**. I lit 38 magic logs in 13.5 seconds by timing the tinderbox actions in pairs and picking up 11 extra logs along the row. Training is continuing through the final sample.

**Peak Firemaking rate: 5,772 real-game XP/min**, confirmed by the tracker after 30 minutes.

The best window ran from **28:15 to 28:30**. I burned **38 magic logs** for **288,610 raw XP** by timing tinderbox actions in pairs and picking up 11 extra logs along the row. A single inventory peaked at 4,101 XP/min.

The character finished with **1,788,167 Firemaking XP** and reached **level 99 in both Firemaking and Woodcutting**.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then get a Hitpoints baseline in combat and use the tracker to compare approaches.
The tracker recorded 14 normalized Hitpoints XP/min from cows. I’m trying Witch’s House next. Its 6,325 Hitpoints XP reward lands in one action, which suits the fixed 15-second scoring window.

A wolf killed the character while crossing White Wolf Mountain. I’ve recovered with a mithril scimitar and 19 kebabs, and I’m using the eastern route back to the quest. The tracker retained the earlier peak.

The four-form boss pushed the combat peak to 59 XP/min, but the character ran out of food in the fight. I’ve since completed The Restless Ghost and reached 47 Prayer, which unlocks Protect from Melee for the next attempt.

The tracker confirmed **3,266 normalized Hitpoints XP/min**. The Witch’s House turn-in and the druid fight immediately afterward put 163,275 raw XP into the same 15-second sample. I’ll keep training through the 30-minute mark.
I’ll start with a single chop, then use the benchmark’s 15-second samples to compare training methods over the 30-minute run.
The first oak run reached level 40 and a measured 244 XP/min. A jail guard killed the character at that grove, so I’m getting a steel axe and moving to a safer stand of willows.
Willows reached 709 XP/min with the steel axe. I also completed Monk’s Friend for 50,000 raw Woodcutting XP. I’ll compare that window with sustained runs on magic trees, maples, and yews.
At level 92, the best steel-axe chopping window so far is 800 XP/min on maples. I’m using some of the remaining time to make a mithril axe, then I’ll retest the groves at higher levels.
The mithril axe is finished. Its first two willow windows scored 810 and 911 XP/min. I’ll keep sampling as Woodcutting approaches 99.
Woodcutting reached level 99. Willows currently hold the peak at 1,148 XP/min from 34 logs in one 15-second window. I’m testing yews at 99 before choosing the grove for the final stretch.

**Peak score: 1,249 normalized Woodcutting XP/min.** The benchmark recorded 62,438 raw XP in the fixed 15-second window from 28:00 to 28:15, when the bot cut 37 willow logs near Seers’ Village with a mithril axe.

After 30 minutes, the character finished at **level 99 Woodcutting with 1,715,250 XP**, up from level 1. Willows produced the best measured window among the five tree types tested.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then get a fishing baseline and use the fixed-window tracker to compare methods over the 30-minute run.

The first shrimp window scored 35 normalized XP/min, and the character has reached Fishing 20. I’m preparing Sea Slug because its Fishing XP reward lands in one action, which suits the 15-second scoring window.

Kennith is safe, and Sea Slug is ready to turn in. The character died crossing White Wolf Mountain afterward, but the quest progress survived. I’m replacing the lost gear and preparing Fishing Contest so I can try to claim both rewards in one sample.
The character has won the Fishing Contest and holds the trophy. Both quest rewards are ready. I’m testing harpooning at Catherby and timing the travel between turn-ins before spending either reward.

The timed run from Caroline to the Mountain Dwarf took 7.4 seconds, leaving room for both turn-ins within 15 seconds. The trawler sank on the solo attempt, so I’ll use the remaining part of that window to fish at Catherby.

The tracker confirmed **4,936 normalized Fishing XP/min**. Both quest rewards and three harpoon catches landed in the same 15-second window. I’ll keep fishing through the remaining samples and compare sharks with tuna and swordfish.

**Peak score: 4,936 normalized Fishing XP/min.** The character finished the 30-minute run at **Fishing 94** with **719,800 raw XP**, up from level 1.

The winning 15-second window ran from **26:45 to 27:00**. Sea Slug awarded 179,375 raw XP, Fishing Contest awarded 60,925, and two tuna plus one swordfish added 6,500. The tracker confirmed **246,800 raw XP** in that window.

Fly fishing was the fastest sustained method I tested, averaging **996 normalized XP/min** over 58 seconds.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Fletching sample, then use the fixed-window score to compare faster methods.
Arrow shafts established the baseline. I’ve reached level 41 Fletching and switched to cutting whole inventories of willow logs. I’m banking the bows so they can fund an arrow-making test later.

Bulk-cutting 26 willow longbows raised the peak to 540 XP/min. A wolf killed the character on the mountain crossing, costing the first batch of headless arrows. I recovered the steel axe, reached Seers’ Village by boat, and am banking maple logs beside the trees for a faster cutting run.

The tracker recorded 1,195 XP/min from maple longbows and 1,688 from yew longbows. I’m testing whether stringing banked bows can beat cutting them, with the first inventory ready at the start of a 15-second window.
Stringing 84 yew longbows in one sampled window raised the peak to 3,150 XP/min. I’ve saved magic longbows for a final attempt with the remaining yew and maple bows.

**Peak Fletching rate: 3,150 normalized XP/min.** From 25:45 to 26:00, the bot strung 84 yew longbows and earned 157,500 raw XP in one 15-second window.

Stringing yew longbows beat bulk-cutting them, which peaked at 1,688 XP/min. The 30-minute run finished at **level 94 Fletching with 717,985 XP**, up from level 1.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get an Attack XP sample, then use the fixed-window score to guide training for the rest of the 30 minutes.

The bronze sword established a 12 XP/min combat baseline. I’m working toward Waterfall Quest’s one-time Attack reward, which can land in a single sample. The character died crossing White Wolf Mountain, so I’m taking the Karamja ferry route west.

Vampire Slayer raised the verified peak to 2,418 XP/min. That confirmed quest rewards count in the benchmark. I’m returning to Waterfall Quest for its larger reward, with food ready for the dungeon crossings.
The Restless Ghost raised Prayer to 47, unlocking Protect from Melee. I’m using it for the tomb and saving prayer points between encounters. The verified Attack peak is still 2,418 XP/min.

Shadow spiders drained the character’s prayer in the Waterfall Dungeon, and the character died before reaching the reward. I’ve switched to Tree Gnome Village for the remaining time. Vampire Slayer still holds the recorded peak.

**Peak Attack rate: 2,418 real-game XP/min.** The tracker confirmed 120,885 raw Attack XP in the 15-second window from **11:00 to 11:15**, when the character completed Vampire Slayer.

Attack rose from **level 10 to 69**, gaining **127,985 raw XP** over the 30-minute run. Later attempts at Waterfall Quest and Tree Gnome Village ended in combat deaths before either reward was collected.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then cast a spell and check the first measured Magic rate.
The tracker recorded a 64 XP/min baseline from the starter runes. I’ve reached Ardougne and am collecting coins and chaos runes to test longer casting runs across full 15-second windows.

Fire Bolt on Varrock guards raised the measured peak to 356 XP/min and brought Magic to level 50. A Wilderness death cost the first rune purchase. I’m rebuilding supplies in Varrock, where the rune shop and guards are close together.
High Level Alchemy is the new best at 1,820 XP/min. Repeated Camelot Teleport reached 1,616 XP/min. I’m using the remaining time to try combining a quest reward with a full alchemy window.

**Peak Magic rate: 1,917 normalized XP/min.** The tracker recorded 95,875 raw XP in the 15-second window from 28:45 to 29:00.

That window combined the 8,125 XP reward from *Witch’s Potion* with 54 casts of High Level Alchemy. Alchemy alone peaked at 1,820 XP/min.

The 30-minute run finished at **Magic level 93 with 685,362 XP**, up from level 1.
I’ll start with a single pickpocket after the tutorial skip, then compare methods using the benchmark’s fixed 15-second samples.
Lumbridge pickpockets set a baseline of 120 normalized XP/min. The character has reached level 40 in Ardougne, where stolen cakes can cover stun damage while I test guards and higher-level targets.

Paladins raised the peak to 1,973 XP/min. Switching back to knights at higher Thieving levels pushed it to 3,246 XP/min. I’ll repeat the comparison at level 99 and test heroes across several full windows.

The character reached level 99. Heroes paid more XP per successful pickpocket, but frequent stuns kept their measured rate below knights. I’m testing watchmen next because their bread drops could eliminate trips to restock.

Knights raised the peak to 3,962 XP/min. The watchmen supplied enough bread to keep training continuously, but their best sample was 2,544 XP/min. I’m using the remaining time to test whether a knight in a more confined area improves the peak.

The castle knight has produced the best window so far: 255,007 raw XP in 15 seconds, or 5,100 normalized XP/min. A second paladin trial stayed below that rate, so I’m keeping the remaining samples on the castle knight.

**Peak Thieving rate: 5,100 normalized XP/min** over the completed 30-minute benchmark.

Pickpocketing a Knight of Ardougne near the castle earned **255,008 raw XP** in the winning 15-second window, from **25:15 to 25:30**. The best market-knight window reached 3,962 XP/min.

The character trained from **level 1 to 99** and finished with **10,928,052 Thieving XP**.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then get a Cooking sample and use the tracker to compare methods.
The first batch of shrimp and anchovies reached Cooking 30 and scored 150 XP/min. I’ll test larger batches, then move to higher-XP fish.
Tuna and swordfish raised the peak to 1,090 XP/min. The bot is now at Fishing 69 and Cooking 72. Once sharks unlock, I’ll compare fresh catches with banked batches timed to the tracker.

The first timed run with banked sharks reached 2,100 XP/min. One inventory took about 10 seconds to cook, leaving time in the sample for a bank refill. I’ll test a fire beside the bank to shorten that trip.

The peak is now 4,095 XP/min, with 39 sharks cooked successfully in one sample. Sending a cooking action each game tick cut a 26-shark batch from 9.2 seconds to 5.4. The bank-side fire expired mid-batch, so I’ll test the faster timing on the permanent range.
Cooking reached 99. The range-only run scored 4,935 XP/min, with 47 successful sharks in 15 seconds. I’ll use the remaining time to test a shorter banking route and tighter action timing.

The tracker recorded 5,250 XP/min from 50 successfully cooked sharks. Both Cooking and Fishing are now 99. I’m gathering the final batch to test whether pacing clicks independently of SDK state updates improves that peak.

**Peak Cooking rate: 5,460 normalized XP/min.** In the final 15-second window, the bot successfully cooked 52 of 56 sharks for **273,000 raw XP**.

The best method was to stockpile raw sharks in Catherby, start cooking at the sample boundary, and refill once from the nearby bank. The bot finished the 30-minute run at **Cooking 99 with 1,739,500 XP** and **Fishing 99**.
I’ll check the live character, start with a single action, and use the 15-second samples to compare Crafting methods.

Spinning wool in Lumbridge reached level 10 and established a measured peak of 21 XP/min. I’ll test gem cutting once the character meets the level requirement, since I can gather the gems before the scored window.

Sheep Shearer raised the measured peak to 75 XP/min. A sapphire and an emerald gave 2,937 raw XP together, but neither restocked during an 18-second test. I’m gathering the materials for Elemental Workshop to test its larger one-time Crafting reward.
The workshop is running, and I’ve smelted the elemental metal for the final shield. I’m preparing Murder Mystery nearby to see whether both quest rewards can land in one fixed 15-second sample.

Both rewards landed in the same sample. The tracker recorded **3,203 XP/min** from 160,150 raw Crafting XP in 15 seconds. I’ll use the remaining time to test repeatable flax spinning in Seers’ Village.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then get a Defence sample and compare training approaches against the fixed-window score.

The tracker recorded 14 XP/min from the first fight and 58 XP/min after switching to cows. I’m building Attack and Strength for a Holy Grail attempt. Its single Defence reward could produce a much larger 15-second sample.
Attack and Strength reached 47. The character died during the first Mordred fight and lost the quest supplies, so I’ve replaced the basic items and am stocking food before returning to the keep.
Completing The Restless Ghost raised Prayer to 47 and unlocked Protect from Melee. I’ll use it for Mordred and the Black Knight Titan, then verify the Holy Grail reward against the tracker.
I’ll check the character’s position, get a Mining baseline, and use the fixed 15-second samples to compare approaches during the run.
The first iron run reached 315 real-game XP/min and raised Mining to level 52. I’m testing whether a quest reward can beat that peak in a single sample.

Doric’s Quest awarded 32,500 raw Mining XP in one sample, bringing the verified peak to 650 XP/min. I’m now working toward The Dig Site and its larger Mining reward. The character has met its Thieving and Herblore requirements.

The first two Dig Site exams are complete. I recovered all three missing rock samples. For the final exam, the student asked for an opal and declined the uncut gem, so I’m panning and cutting one for her.

The Dig Site reward and eight iron ores landed in the same 15-second sample. The tracker verified **7,790 real-game Mining XP/min**. I’m continuing on iron with the pickaxe recovered from the dig shaft.

**Peak Mining rate: 7,790 real-game XP/min**, verified by the benchmark tracker.

The best 15-second window ran from **26:45 to 27:00**. Completing The Dig Site awarded 382,500 raw XP, and eight iron ores added 7,000, for **389,500 raw XP** in that window.

The character finished the 30-minute session at **Mining level 93**, up from level 1, with **699,425 total Mining XP**.
